mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in the federal funds rate over three consecutive months signals a tightening monetary policy stance, raising discount rates and reducing present value of future corporate cash flows, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS rises by >0.25% per month for 3 consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -0.5%) in at least 70% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A year-over-year decline in real personal consumption expenditures (proxied by GDPC1) exceeding 2% coincident with a rise in unemployment (UNRATE) above 6% signals a demand contraction, which depresses corporate earnings and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly increase in payroll employment (PAYEMS) of at least 50,000 persons for four consecutive months signals robust labor market expansion, which boosts consumer demand and corporate profit margins, resulting in positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS rises by >50,000 for 4 consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly above zero (< +0.5%) in at least 60% of triggered months.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly decline in the industrial production index (INDPRO) of more than 0.5% for three consecutive months indicates weakening manufacturing activity, which reduces corporate revenues and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -0.5%) in at least 60% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A concurrent rise in the housing starts index (HOUST) and real personal savings (RSAFS) above their respective 12-month moving averages signals increased household investment and liquidity, which supports consumer spending and drives positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly positive (> +0.7%) in at least 55% of triggered quarters.

mechanism_narrative: A federal funds rate held below 1% for more than six consecutive months during a period of positive GDP growth (GDPC1) signals accommodative monetary policy, which lowers borrowing costs and boosts equity valuations, resulting in positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS < 1% for >6 months and GDPC1 growth >0%
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly above zero (< +0.6%) in at least 60% of triggered quarters.

mechanism_narrative: A rapid deceleration in unemployment rate (UNRATE) to below 4% while payroll employment (PAYEMS) growth slows sharply indicates labor market overheating followed by cooling, which often precedes a recession and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE < 4% and PAYEMS growth falls by >30% YoY
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -0.6%) in at least 60% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly increase in real personal consumption expenditures (GDPC1) of more than 0.5% for four consecutive months signals strengthening consumer demand, which lifts corporate revenues and profits, resulting in positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly above zero (< +0.5%) in at least 60% of triggered months.
